name: Tsinghua University
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Students with a Chinese passport are not allowed to apply to this university
  • Good level in math required


Tsinghua University

When it was created in 1911, Tsinghua was initially a preparatory school for Chinese students wishing to do a second cycle at American universities. In 1925, it developed into a full-fledged university and now offers undergraduate and graduate degree programs.

For decades, Tsinghua University has been considered the "MIT of China." Beginning in the late 1980s, the state began to design a new Tsinghua that included more diverse disciplines. By April of 2005, the university was able to develop 13 faculties, 54 departments, 41 research institutes, 35 research centers, and 171 laboratories; including 12 national laboratories and 15 laboratories of the Ministry of Education.


Currently, among the 7,800 teachers at Tsinghua, there is a Nobel Prize winner (Zhenning Yang), a Turing Prize winner (Qizhi Yao), thirty-five members of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and thirty-one members of the Chinese Academy of Engineering.

Many students study at Tsinghua: 13,000 undergraduates, 13,000 masters, 5,000 doctoral, 1,700 foreigners from 46 countries and 9,000 through correspondence education courses.


For Chinese high school students, Tsinghua is one of two mainland universities with the most selective admissions process. Each year in all provinces, those admitted are only those with the best marks. After studying for the bachelor's degree, a considerable part of Tsinghua's students will pursue their doctoral work at American universities.


At Tsinghua, "Action is more important than words," and the school motto emphasizes everyone's constant efforts and high moral standards.


Among the eminent alumni of Tsinghua we find political leaders, great scientists, and the leaders of important companies. For example, Xi Jinping, the current President of the People's Republic of China; Jiaxian Deng, "the father of China's two nuclear bombs"; and Zhang Chaoyang, the creator of the Sohu website and the CEO of Sohu, one of the first Internet portals in China.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.


Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Create an account and then apply directly online. After completing all the steps online, download the entire completed form ("Foreigner's Application Form for Admission to Graduate Programs”), then sign and upload the completed form, not forgetting to include your photo).
  • Motivation letter in English
  • Epitech school certificate in English
  • Transcripts in English (available on your intra)
  • 2 letters of recommendation from teachers in English with their telephone and email details indicated at the bottom of the page
  • Tepitech score certificate downloadable from the intra
  • 180 ECTS certificate document (ask the AFFI team)
  • Copy of your passport

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Acceptance letter

Once you've submitted your application, your host university will review your documents.

You will then receive an acceptance letter (might take a few weeks), mandatory to apply for a visa.


3. Visa application

You must take the necessary steps in obtaining a study visa type X1 upon receipt of the letter of admission and the form JW202 (sent to you by email). Please check this site for more information. Price: between 110 and 130€ (2025). You can also entrust the file to an agency by clicking here.


The X1 visa is an entry visa valid for 3 months from the date of entry into China. After your arrival, you must obtain a Chinese residence permit within 30 days of entering China.


The host university will assist you with visa conversion procedures, medical examinations, and obtaining the resident permit.

Related costs are the responsibility of the students (see estimated budget at the bottom of the page).


Please note:

  • For the latest information regarding visa application, you should contact your nearest Embassy/Consulate of China.
  • After you arrive in the Chinese mainland, the X visa for single entry cannot allow you to exit and re-enter the Chinese mainland. You must stay in the Chinese mainland until the Residence Permit is granted.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "For the Visa, I got my visa in less than a week after making my demand by going to the Chinese Visa center of Marseille which has a usual delay of < 1 week, with no need to book a meeting in advance. I would not recommend going to the Visa center of Paris, as the delay is much higher (expect at least 2 weeks in addition to having to book a meeting with them ahead)."


4. Insurance and health

You will be asked to undergo medical examinations after arriving in Beijing.

The results must be presented to the Beijing Bureau of Exit and Entry Administration of the Ministry of Public Security when you apply for a residence permit.


The costs of these exams will be borne by the student (see “Estimated Budget”).


According to the regulations made by Chinese Ministry of Education, all the international students in China are required to purchase comprehensive insurance and the valid period should cover the duration of their studies.


In order to be fully covered for medical care, we recommend that you take out international insurance as well. It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Although Tsinghua requires a medical certificate along with blood test and vaccines to be done ahead of arriving in China, nearly every foreign student needs to undergo another medical test upon arriving, which leads me to believe that doing the medical exam before arriving in China is not mandatory and is not taken into account."


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/chine

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


5.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on China, click here.

Student's feedback regarding what to anticipate for your arrival at Tsinghua (2024-2025): "When arriving in Tsinghua University, foreign students will need to register. To do that, they will go in front of Building 23 where all other foreign students will also be, that way, you just have to follow the others. There will a be quick lesson on how to prevent fires, use an extinguisher and what practices are forbidden in order to avoid a fire. After finishing that test, you will need to bring the documents you had to prepare (such as a photocopy of your passport, some cash for the administrative fees) and that were mentionned in the mails you received. Some documents will have to be obtained directly on site.


The medical certifiate is not mandatory to start registering and obtain your dormitory room key. It will however, be needed to finalize the registration later on. To obtain your dormitory room key, simply go to the the building you booked a room in and present your registration documents to the reception.


It is not possible to go to the campus restaurant without a student ID. If you want to eat and don't know any student that can help you, you can still go to the multiple supermarkets on campus and pay either by cash or WeChat/Alipay.


After the first day, you will need to go the health center to undergo the medical exam. There are two days, generally the first Thursday and first Friday, where all foreign students will go to the center. You can organize between students to take a taxi or didi (chinese equivalent of uber).


It will also be from Thirsday to Friday that the course registration platform will open. Bear in mind that slots go extremely fast and are limited. Be prepared to be in a place with a good connection and on your computer at the exact time the platform opens.


Classes only start the second week. You have one week to accommodate and adapt to the Chinese lifestyle before starting to study. During week one, a​ big meeting will be organized on campus where all foreign students must go. They will communicate informations relative to campus life. Do not worry, all these informations will be communicated either by the management team the first day, or via wechat in the groups they will have make you join."
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

Accommodations are provided in an on-campus dormitory. Due to limited space in campus dorms, rooms on campus are reserved only for those who have applied directly to the university before the stated deadline.


Booking instructions are provided in the admission package sent by Tsinghua.


You can choose between three types of rooms:

  • Single room (bathroom and private toilet)
  • Room AB (bathroom and toilet shared with the flat mate)
  • Double rooms (bathroom and toilet shared).

In each room you will find sheets, color TV, air conditioning, telephone and internet access.


Plan 300 euros per month for a single room (with private bathroom) with cleaning service and bedding. You can find Information on the dormitory here: http://ac.cs.tsinghua.edu.cn/accomodation.html

Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Foreign students and Chinese students are not in the same building, except for some very special cases.


There are two types of room : AB room and double rooms.

Double rooms contain 2 people and is a single room. There is a big shower room per floor shared by all people from that floor.

AB Rooms have a bathroom in them, and separate bedrooms. They contain 2 people. This type of room is not going to exist for a long time as they are getting replaced by double rooms. They also cost twice as much as Double rooms.

Depending on the building, some double rooms have sinks in them and bunk beds, while other have distinct beds, but no sinks.

Building 23 : Mixed building with men on floor 1 to 6 and women on floor 7 to 12. Distinc beds, no sink.

Building 22 : Only men. Bunk beds, sink.

Building 21 : Currently on renovation.

Building 20 : AB rooms.

Building 19 : Same as building 21, only women


I would recommend taking a double room for economic reason, and because double rooms are visually more pleasant than AB rooms, except for people that specifically cannot withstand having a shared room.

For the building, I would recommend taking building 22 or 19 as having a sink is very useful to brush your teeth and other things without having to go out. But for those that prefer separate beds and more space, then building 23 is the best option."


Off-campus acommodation (more information here)

Due to limited amount of accommodation available on campus, some students will need to live off-campus and arrange accommodation in advance. 

Notes:

  • always keep copies of all payments and the contract
  • always sign a contract. Without a contract you have no legal rights
  • when you live off-campus, never forget to register at your local police station to obtain a Registration Form of Temporary Residence within 24 hours after your arrival in China or signing of the rental contract.


Finding accommodation via reputable rental agencies

Due to its close proximity to Tsinghua University, many students living off campus choose to live in apartment blocks located in the Wudaokou and Liudaokou areas


Below are the main rental agencies in China. Before your arrival, you can first access their websites to learn of their accommodation options. Then once in China, you can go to their neighborhood shopfronts to request to view properties.


  • Ziroom is a popular choice for foreigners renting in Beijing. They have an easy-to-use app that also has an English interface for searching for accommodation. Once securing accommodation via Ziroom, on the app you can find the details of your accommodation, including the contract and details on your payments made. Included in the contract is a service fee, which includes regular cleaning of the public spaces of the apartment, and also easy servicing for repairs. You will also be advised to add your agent on WeChat for ease of contact.

courses:
Credits

Students must validate 15 local credits for the 1st semester and 12 local credits for the 2nd semester among the courses below.


Academic calendar (2025-2026)

Fall semester: Sept 15-Jan 19 or 22

Spring semester: Feb 15-June 30


Department and courses

Tsinghua University offers 2 programs to our students and will decide in which program you will be accepted according to the profile of each applicant.


Epitech students admitted as "visiting students" will take classes in the Master in Advanced Computing program of the Computer Science and Technology department.

  • Chinese Language (2 credits)
  • Overview of China (2 credits)
  • Combinatorics and Algorithms Design (4 credits)
  • Advanced Machine Learning (3 credits)
  • Web Information Retrieval (3 credits)
  • Future Internet (3 credits)
  • Distributed Database Systems (3 credits)
  • Human Computer Interaction Technologies (3 credits)
  • Fundamentals of Computer Graphics (3 credits)
  • Topics in Advanced Multimedia Technologies (3 credits)
  • Process and Methods of Software Project Management (3 credit)
  • Introduction to big data systems (3 credits)
  • Advanced Network Management (3 credits)
  • Distributed Systems (3 credits)
  • Network Security (2 credits)
  • Natural Language Processing (3 credits)
  • Deep Learning (3 credits)

You will find the list of courses here.


Course format and workload

The mathematics courses are very high level, and we urge each candidate to take this element into account when choosing Tsinghua University.


Student's feedback (2024-2025): "Courses in Tsinghua can be overwhelming or relatively easy based on what kind of classes you take. It is true that the expected math level is high, but definitively not out of range for a dedicated student (I am talking about students that want to learn and improve, not necessarily the students with a social life). Chinese classes are available for different levels--from beginner (A1 / HSK1), intermediate (B1 / HSK 3) to advanced (A1~A2 / HSK5).

The first week, you can register and unregister from any class you want, as long as it has enough slots. This way, you can try classes you are not sure to be fit for, and even go to classes you are not registered for.


Past that delay, you will need to make a special demand to register to some courses, which is done via the same platform, altough this time, the teacher will need to manually accept your demand instead of being registered right away.


If you want to register for a class that has no more slots, you can go to the FIT building in Tsinghua, and go talk to the foreign students manager, and give her your name and student ID, so that, if any slots is free, you will automatically be registered.

The hardest classes in Tsinghua are definitively the ones about AI (Machine Learning, Deep learning, NLP, ...). These will need a lot of investment and the homework will take a lot of time. I do not recommend taking 2 or more, except if the classes didn't seem overwhelming during the first week.


Most classes take ~2h30 per week, so to get the number of credits required by Epitech, you will usually just go to class in the morning and have a free afternoon. This is because Chinese teachers expect you to work much more out of class than during class. Some classes will have homework, some will have projects, and they will either have a final exam and mid-term exam, or have a final project (like Epitech)."

Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Insurance from Tsinghua: 78€, 300-600€ for additional insurance contract depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Administrative fees and other expenses: at least 800yuan in cash (100€) according to a former student (2024-2025), etc.


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Yuan (RMB or CNY). 1 € = 8.26 RMB (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

  • Housing: 600€/semester (double rooms), 1200€/semester (AB rooms)
  • Food : 70€ / month (only eating at campus restaurants), 100€ / month (campus restaurants most of the time + some restaurants outside)
  • Transportation: 25-30€ for a second-hand bike
  • Phone, internet: 16€ internet/ 6€ phone
  • If you’re with Free Mobile, their €20/month plan includes some roaming data in China, which can be very helpful for the first few days. Otherwise, you can easily buy a local eSIM or a China Unicom SIM card at the airport for short-term use.
  • Leisure: 200€ (1-week trip with normal trains, restaurants, museums, etc.) or 500€ (1-week trip with plane or high-speed train)

These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.
